newsitem.title: FINLAND: Amer says targets break-even in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Amer says targets break-even in 1997.

text.p: Finnish sporting goods group Amer-yhtyma Oy is targetting a break-even result in 1997, it said in a company bulletin received on Monday.
"We intend to reach break-even in the next financial year," it quoted Amer CEO Roger Talermo as saying.
On October 10, Amer said it expected full-year 1996 earnings before extraordinary items and tax to fall to a clear loss from a 142 million markka profit in 1995.
Amer's January-August result before extraordinaries and tax was a 206 million markka loss, down from a 36 million markka profit in the first eight-months of 1995.
Talermo said in June that Amer aims to show a profit in 1997.
"Our definite goal is to make a profitable result in 1997," Talermo said in an interview in a company newsletter received on June 20.
